question: Should requester-consumed descendant output be treated as terminal delivery proof for the exact matched descendant runs, including when the final outward cron delivery later fails?
rationale: This PR deliberately changes subagent delivery semantics and persisted restore behavior; tests can verify mechanics, but only maintainer intent can decide whether requester consumption is the accepted delivery boundary.

options.title: Require rebase, proof, and semantic sign-off
options.body: Ask the author to preserve current generation-aware dedupe, add real runtime/restore proof, and then decide the requester-consumption delivery boundary before merge.

options.title: Accept requester-consumed delivery semantics
options.body: Maintain the PR direction after rebase if maintainers agree exact matched requester consumption should suppress descendant retry/finalization.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this PR if the remaining desired model is a durable completion inbox/spool rather than a requester-consumption terminal credit path.

recommendation.title: Require rebase, proof, and semantic sign-off
recommendation.body: Ask the author to preserve current generation-aware dedupe, add real runtime/restore proof, and then decide the requester-consumption delivery boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the deterministic subagent announce-delivery and descendant-gating surface introduced in the merged feature history.
